reports.full_content:
# Structured Latents (SLAT) and O-Voxel Representation

The community consists of two entities: Structured Latents (SLAT) and O-Voxel Representation. SLAT is a latent encoding attached to active voxels encoding geometry and texture, while O-Voxel Representation is a field-free sparse voxel structure encoding geometry and appearance jointly. SLAT is the latent encoding of the O-Voxel representation, indicating a component relationship between the two entities.

## SLAT as latent encoding of O-Voxel Representation

Structured Latents (SLAT) serves as the latent encoding attached to active voxels that encode geometry and texture. This encoding is specifically the latent encoding of the O-Voxel representation, establishing SLAT as a foundational component of the voxel structure. The relationship between these entities is defined as HAS_COMPONENT, where SLAT is the latent encoding of the O-Voxel representation [Data: Entities (30, 31); Relationships (19)]. This component relationship suggests that SLAT provides the underlying latent structure that enables the O-Voxel representation to function as a field-free sparse voxel structure encoding geometry and appearance jointly.

## O-Voxel Representation as field-free sparse voxel structure

O-Voxel Representation is described as a field-free sparse voxel structure that encodes geometry and appearance jointly. This entity represents the structural framework that utilizes the latent encoding provided by SLAT. The field-free nature of this representation suggests computational efficiency in encoding spatial information, while the joint encoding of geometry and appearance indicates a unified approach to representing voxel data [Data: Entities (31); Relationships (19)]. The sparse nature of the voxel structure implies that it efficiently represents only active voxels, which aligns with SLAT being attached to active voxels specifically.

## Component relationship between SLAT and O-Voxel Representation

The HAS_COMPONENT relationship between SLAT and O-Voxel Representation indicates that SLAT is a constituent part of the O-Voxel system. This relationship has a combined degree of 4, suggesting moderate connectivity within the broader network context [Data: Relationships (19)]. SLAT's degree of 3 indicates it has multiple connections, while O-Voxel Representation's degree of 1 suggests it is more specialized in its connections. This asymmetry in degrees implies that SLAT may serve as a more central or versatile encoding mechanism, while O-Voxel Representation is a specific application of that encoding.

## Technical capabilities of the voxel encoding system

The combination of SLAT and O-Voxel Representation creates a technical system for encoding 3D geometric and appearance data. SLAT provides latent encodings attached to active voxels, while O-Voxel Representation structures these encodings into a field-free sparse voxel format. This system appears designed for efficient representation of spatial data where both geometric structure and visual appearance are encoded together in a sparse format [Data: Entities (30, 31); Relationships (19)]. The field-free approach suggests avoidance of continuous field representations in favor of discrete voxel-based encoding, which may offer advantages in computational efficiency and memory usage for certain applications.

## Network centrality and connectivity patterns

SLAT has a degree of 3, indicating it connects to multiple entities in the network, while O-Voxel Representation has a degree of 1, suggesting it is more peripheral or specialized. The relationship between them has a combined degree of 4, reflecting the cumulative connectivity of this pair [Data: Entities (30, 31); Relationships (19)]. These degree metrics suggest that SLAT may play a more central role in the broader network of entities, potentially serving as an encoding mechanism used by multiple systems, while O-Voxel Representation is a specific implementation focused on sparse voxel structures.

reports.title: TETRIS3D Framework and Associated Research Community
reports.summary: The TETRIS3D community centers on the TETRIS3D framework, a 3D scene generation system built on TRELLIS.2 that reconstructs object-centric 3D scenes from single images. The framework generates objects autoregressively, explicitly conditioning each on neighboring geometry and physical relations to ensure geometric and physical coherence. The community encompasses related entities including evaluation datasets (Toys4K), foundational methods (TRELLIS, QWEN3-VL-30B), evaluation metrics (reconstruction quality, physical stability), and various research components spanning spatial context, depth mapping, and visible-to-invisible attention mechanisms. TETRIS3D is evaluated across multiple benchmarks including real-world scene benchmarks and synthetic datasets, with comparisons to baselines including GPT-6 Astra and Axolotl3D. The framework incorporates a two-stage pipeline of sparse structure and structured latent generation, with approximately 1.83B and 1.68B parameters respectively. reports.full_content:
# TETRIS3D Framework and Associated Research Community

The TETRIS3D community centers on the TETRIS3D framework, a 3D scene generation system built on TRELLIS.2 that reconstructs object-centric 3D scenes from single images. The framework generates objects autoregressively, explicitly conditioning each on neighboring geometry and physical relations to ensure geometric and physical coherence. The community encompasses related entities including evaluation datasets (Toys4K), foundational methods (TRELLIS, QWEN3-VL-30B), evaluation metrics (reconstruction quality, physical stability), and various research components spanning spatial context, depth mapping, and visible-to-invisible attention mechanisms. TETRIS3D is evaluated across multiple benchmarks including real-world scene benchmarks and synthetic datasets, with comparisons to baselines including GPT-6 Astra and Axolotl3D. The framework incorporates a two-stage pipeline of sparse structure and structured latent generation, with approximately 1.83B and 1.68B parameters respectively. Relationships show TETRIS3D's connections to evaluation datasets, foundational models, physical reasoning components, and quality metrics, forming a comprehensive ecosystem for 3D scene generation research.

## TETRIS3D as the central framework for 3D scene generation

TETRIS3D serves as the foundational entity within this community, representing a 3D scene generation framework introduced in the paper 'TETRIS3D: 3D SCENE GENERATION WITH OBJECTS THAT FIT TOGETHER.' Built on TRELLIS.2, the framework generates objects autoregressively while explicitly conditioning each object on neighboring geometry and physical relations to achieve geometric and physical coherence. The framework utilizes a two-stage pipeline consisting of sparse structure generation (approximately 1.83B parameters) and structured latent generation (approximately 1.68B parameters), with visible-to-invisible attention layers designed to faithfully complete occluded parts. This central role is supported by entity record 1 and relationship records 101, 31, 235, 286, and 1 showing TETRIS3D's connections to evaluation datasets, spatial context, penetration depth metrics, reconstruction quality reporting, and inter-object spatial compatibility features respectively [Data: Entities (159); Relationships (101, 31, 235, 286, 1)].

## Evaluation on Toys4K and related datasets

TETRIS3D is extensively evaluated on the Toys4K dataset, which serves as a comprehensive evaluation resource used across multiple analyses in associated research. The evaluation encompasses quantitative comparisons in Tables 1, 4, and 5, qualitative results in Figure 4, and qualitative comparisons with baselines. Beyond Toys4K, TETRIS3D is also evaluated on real-world scene benchmarks including those from Stojanov et al. (2021), Ansari et al. (2026), and Yu et al. (2026), as well as synthetic scenes. The framework reports superior performance across reconstruction quality, generation quality, and physical stability metrics, with one experiment specifically using VLM-inferred relations while another assesses sensitivity to depth estimation errors by replacing ground-truth depth maps with predictions from MoGe3. This evaluation scope is supported by entity records 108 and 156, and relationship records 101, 10, 11, 12, and 243 showing TETRIS3D's connections to Toys4K, VLM-based physical relation reasoning, and real-world scene benchmarks respectively [Data: Entities (108, 156); Relationships (101, 10, 11, 12, 243)].

## Physical reasoning and spatial context mechanisms

A core component of TETRIS3D involves explicit physical reasoning about how objects should rest on or fit within their neighbors. The framework incorporates spatial context that captures the geometric arrangement of neighboring objects relative to the target object, thereby discouraging interpenetration and floating to ensure physical plausibility. Physical relationships are explicitly conditioned on, with the system using a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to infer a physical dependency hierarchy and derive generation order through topological sorting. The framework also employs per-token injection mechanisms that derive conditions from depth maps, back-projected image features, and object interactions on the same 3D grid. These physical reasoning components are supported by entity records 42, 15, 39, 8, and 26, and relationship records 3, 235, 26, 8, and 26 showing TETRIS3D's connections to spatial context, physical stability metrics, VLM usage, foundational method references, and built-on relationships respectively [Data: Entities (42, 15, 39, 8, 26); Relationships (3, 235, 26, 8, 26)].

## Quality metrics and evaluation capabilities

TETRIS3D reports multiple quality metrics including scene-level quality (CD-S, F1-S, ICP-Rot), object-level quality (CD-O), and physical stability metrics (PD, DMEAN). The framework achieves superior performance in physical stability by analyzing inter-object penetration and post-simulation stability, ensuring objects maintain realistic physical interactions. Additional metrics include residual rotation error after per-object ICP alignment and mean displacement measuring settling error. These quality metrics draw from various sources including Achlioptas et al. (2018) for MMD and COV generative quality metrics, Nichol et al. (2022) for P-FID generative quality metric, and Lee et al. (2026) and Li et al. (2026B) for physical stability metrics. The system's reporting capabilities are extensive, with 18 different quality metrics documented across relationship records 227-236, supported by entity records 143, 144, 145, 146, and 147-150 [Data: Entities (143, 144, 145, 146, 147-150); Relationships (227-236)].

## Architectural components and training infrastructure

TETRIS3D incorporates several key architectural components including QWEN3-VL-30B for object instance extraction and physical relation inference, VISIBLE-TO-INVISIBLE (V2I) ATTENTION for faithful completion of occluded parts, and per-token nearest-surface conditions used by lightweight encoders in each block. The framework is built on NVIDIA H200 GPUs using the AdamW optimizer and employs classifier-free guidance through condition dropout. Training follows a two-stage curriculum strategy with Stage 1 and Stage 2, incorporating depth augmentation and observed depth points trained with Gaussian noise perturbation. The architecture also includes components like Π (projecting voxel centers), unsigned distance fields, direction vectors, surface normals, and relation type embeddings. These components are supported by entity records 271, 159, 218, 314, and 315, and relationship records 344, 199, 303, 314, and 315 showing TETRIS3D's connections to vision-language models, attention mechanisms, GPU infrastructure, and training strategies respectively [Data: Entities (271, 159, 218, 314, 315); Relationships (344, 199, 303, 314, 315)].

## Comparisons with baselines and related methods

TETRIS3D is compared against multiple baselines and related methods in the research ecosystem. The framework shows superior performance compared to existing methods across reconstruction quality, generation quality, and physical stability metrics. Comparisons include agentic generation tools like GPT-6 Astra, and methods following Axolotl3D's synthetic occlusion protocol. The framework has also been evaluated against large-scale 3D datasets referenced from Deitke et al. (2023B;A) and shape encoding approaches from Zhang et al. (2023; 2024; Li et al., 2025; Zhao et al., 2025B), latents-to-3D asset approaches from Xiang et al. (2025; Wu et al., 2026; Xiang et al., 2026), and image feature injection methods from Cheng et al. (2023; Hong et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025; Chen et al., 2026B). These comparisons establish TETRIS3D's competitive positioning within the 3D scene generation field, supported by relationship records 218, 291, 292, 293, and 294 showing comparison relationships [Data: Relationships (218, 291, 292, 293, 294)].

## Real-world benchmark evaluations

TETRIS3D has been evaluated on real-world scene benchmarks containing complex interactions and contacts, demonstrating its capability to handle challenging real-world scenarios. The framework's performance on these benchmarks contributes to its reputation as a robust 3D scene generation system. Real-world scene benchmarks serve as evaluation contexts alongside synthetic datasets, with the framework being tested on configurations from various research groups including Lee et al. (2026) and Li et al. (2026B) for physical stability metrics. This real-world evaluation capability is supported by entity record 153 and relationship records 243, 244, and 245 showing TETRIS3D's evaluation on real-world scene benchmarks and its use of VLM-based physical relation reasoning with estimated depth [Data: Entities (153); Relationships (243, 244, 245)].

## Depth mapping and image feature integration

TETRIS3D generates each object directly in the pose observed in the scene image using both depth maps and image feature back-projection. The depth map is used in conjunction with image feature back-projection to generate objects in the poses observed in the scene image. The framework also incorporates depth augmentation during training, using Gaussian noise to perturb observed depth points, and trains on observed depth points as a conditioning signal. These depth-related mechanisms are fundamental to the framework's ability to reconstruct object poses accurately, supported by entity records 40, 41, 244, and 245, and relationship records 29, 30, 327, and 328 showing TETRIS3D's use of depth maps, image feature back-projection, depth augmentation, and observed depth points respectively [Data: Entities (40, 41); Relationships (29, 30, 327, 328)].

## Integration with TRELLIS and foundational methods

TETRIS3D is built on TRELLIS, which serves as a preliminaries method referenced in the paper's preliminary sections and also functions as a reference method for rendering configurations. The framework's architectural foundation leverages TRELLIS's capabilities, with relationship records showing the built-on relationship between TETRIS3D and TRELLIS. This integration with foundational methods extends to various research references including large-scale 3D datasets, shape encoding approaches, latents-to-3D asset decoding methods, and image feature injection techniques. The TRELLIS integration provides the foundational framework upon which TETRIS3D's object-centric 3D scene generation capabilities are built, supported by entity record 37 and relationship records 26, 28, and 37 showing TETRIS3D's built-on relationship, VLM usage, and foundational method reference respectively [Data: Entities (37); Relationships (26, 28, 37)].

## Community research scope and future directions

The TETRIS3D community encompasses a broad research scope spanning 3D scene generation, physical reasoning, evaluation metrics, and comparisons with existing methods. The framework's two-stage pipeline architecture, explicit physical relation conditioning, and VLM-inferred dependency hierarchies represent significant contributions to the field. Future directions may include further refinement of physical stability metrics, expansion of real-world benchmark evaluations, and continued comparisons with emerging generative AI methods. The community's research is documented across 250+ entity records and 350+ relationship records, forming a comprehensive ecosystem for 3D scene generation research that continues to evolve with new methodologies, datasets, and evaluation approaches. This comprehensive research scope is supported by the extensive entity and relationship data showing connections across all major aspects of the framework's development and evaluation [Data: Entities (entire dataset); Relationships (entire dataset)].

# TETRIS3D and V2I ATTENTION

The community centers on the TETRIS3D system and its V2I ATTENTION module, a key architectural component that enables amodal perception and 3D reconstruction. V2I ATTENTION functions within each DiT (Diffusion Transformer) to allow invisible tokens, identified by object masks, to attend to visible tokens via cross-attention. This configuration replaces prior attention modules and supports the system's ability to complete occluded areas. The ablation configuration, W/O V2I ATTN., represents a variant without this module, allowing for performance comparison within the TETRIS3D framework. The relationships illustrate a core system and its critical component, alongside an ablation variant used for system analysis.

## TETRIS3D as the primary system incorporating V2I ATTENTION

TETRIS3D is the central system in this community, described as incorporating V2I ATTENTION as a key component. According to the relationships, TETRIS3D utilizes this V2I attention mechanism, introduced in Section 3.3, to enhance its functionality. The integration of V2I attention within TETRIS3D indicates a specific architectural design choice aimed at improving performance or capabilities related to the system's intended application. This positions TETRIS3D as the primary entity driving the community's focus, as it is the system that houses and employs the attention module. [Data: Relationships (265); Entities (36)]

## V2I ATTENTION as a critical component within DiT architectures

V2I ATTENTION functions as a component within each DiT (Diffusion Transformer), enabling invisible tokens identified by object masks to attend to visible tokens through cross-attention. By aggregating information from visible regions, V2I ATTENTION completes occluded areas, supporting amodal perception and 3D reconstruction tasks. This module replaces a prior attention module in the Amodal3R Attn configuration, marking a significant architectural shift. Its role is technical and foundational, as it enables the core perception capabilities of the system, making it a critical element for understanding the advanced functionality of TETRIS3D. [Data: Entities (36); Relationships (265)]

## The existence and purpose of the ablation configuration W/O V2I ATTN.

The ablation configuration labeled W/O V2I ATTN. represents a variant of TETRIS3D without the V2I attention module. This configuration is constructed from TETRIS3D and serves as a baseline for comparison, allowing researchers to assess the impact of the V2I attention mechanism on system performance. The relationship between W/O V2I ATTN. and TETRIS3D is defined as a constructed ablation configuration, indicating its role in experimental analysis rather than as a standalone system. This setup facilitates the evaluation of how the presence of V2I ATTENTION influences the overall capabilities of the TETRIS3D framework. [Data: Relationships (266); Entities (164)]

## Technical function of cross-attention in amodal perception

The technical operation of V2I ATTENTION relies on cross-attention mechanisms where invisible tokens, identified by object masks, attend to visible tokens. This process allows the system to aggregate information from visible regions to complete occluded areas, thereby supporting amodal perception and 3D reconstruction tasks. The ability to 'invisible tokens' and 'object masks' suggests a sophisticated approach to handling partial or hidden data, which is essential for advanced 3D reconstruction. This technical detail underscores the module's importance in enabling the system to reason about and reconstruct complete 3D structures from incomplete inputs. [Data: Entities (36)]

## Comparative analysis between system variants

The relationship between TETRIS3D and W/O V2I ATTN. enables a comparative analysis of system performance with and without the V2I attention module. By constructing the ablation configuration from TETRIS3D, researchers can isolate the effects of the attention mechanism. This comparative approach is standard in machine learning research to validate the contribution of specific components. The data suggests that the presence of V2I ATTENTION is a deliberate architectural choice in TETRIS3D, and its removal, as demonstrated by the W/O V2I ATTN. configuration, likely results in measurable differences in perception and reconstruction capabilities. [Data: Relationships (265, 266)]

## Role of Section 3.3 in introducing the V2I attention mechanism

The V2I attention mechanism was introduced in Section 3.3 of the associated documentation, marking its formal integration into the TETRIS3D system. This section likely details the theoretical underpinnings and practical implementation of the mechanism. The reference to Section 3.3 provides a specific locus for understanding how the attention module was designed and incorporated into the system's architecture. This contextual information is crucial for understanding the timeline and rationale behind the adoption of V2I ATTENTION in the TETRIS3D framework. [Data: Relationships (265)]

## Degree centrality and connectivity of entities

The entities within this community exhibit varying degrees of connectivity, as indicated by the degree attribute in the entity data. V2I ATTENTION and W/O V2I ATTN. both have a degree of 3, while TETRIS3D is involved in relationships with combined degrees of 162. This disparity highlights TETRIS3D as the highly connected hub of the community, serving as the primary system, whereas the attention module and its ablation variant are more peripheral components or configurations. The degree metrics help quantify the structural importance of each entity within the overall network. [Data: Entities (36, 164); Relationships (265, 266)]

## Configuration and variant naming conventions

The community demonstrates specific naming conventions for system configurations, distinguishing between the primary system (TETRIS3D), the key module (V2I ATTENTION), and the ablation variant (W/O V2I ATTN.). These names clearly denote the relationship and hierarchical structure between the entities. The 'W/O' prefix explicitly indicates 'without', establishing the ablation configuration as a derivative work based on the removal of the specified module. Such naming conventions are essential for clarity in technical documentation and research reproducibility. [Data: Entities (36, 164); Relationships (265, 266)]

## Potential impact on 3D reconstruction and perception tasks

The primary implication of the V2I ATTENTION module within TETRIS3D is its support for amodal perception and 3D reconstruction tasks. By enabling the completion of occluded areas through the aggregation of visible region information, the module directly impacts the system's ability to accurately reconstruct 3D structures. The technical capabilities of V2I ATTENTION suggest that it is a significant advancement in handling incomplete data, which has broad applications in computer vision and robotics. The community's focus on these capabilities indicates a drive towards more robust and accurate 3D modeling solutions. [Data: Entities (36)]

# Bounding-Box IoU (IOU-B) and Single Rigid ICP Transformation

The community consists of two key entities: Bounding-Box IoU (IOU-B), a scene-level quality metric, and Single Rigid ICP Transformation, an alignment method. The relationship indicates that IOU-B uses a single rigid ICP transformation to align the predicted scene to the ground-truth scene before calculating the metric.

## Bounding-Box IoU (IOU-B) as a scene-level quality metric

Bounding-Box IoU (IOU-B) is a scene-level quality metric that measures the volumetric intersection-over-union between axis-aligned bounding boxes of aligned predicted and ground-truth point sets. This metric is used to evaluate the accuracy of scene alignment and object detection in computer vision applications. [Data: Entities (140)]

## Single Rigid ICP Transformation as an alignment method

Single Rigid ICP Transformation is an alignment method used to align the predicted scene to the ground-truth scene before computing IoU-B. The Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm is a widely used method for aligning 3D point clouds, and the rigid transformation ensures that the alignment preserves the shape and size of the objects. [Data: Entities (287)]

## Relationship between IOU-B and Single Rigid ICP Transformation

The relationship between IOU-B and Single Rigid ICP Transformation indicates that IOU-B uses a single rigid ICP transformation to align the predicted scene to the ground-truth scene. This relationship highlights the importance of accurate scene alignment in computing the IoU-B metric. [Data: Relationships (357)]

reports.full_content:
# TETRIS3D and Blender 3D Scene Generation Community

The community centers on TETRIS3D, a 3D scene generation method that constructs scenes with objects that fit together. TETRIS3D uses Blender and CPU for execution, incorporates containment object primitives such as CUPS, OPEN BINS, POLYGONAL BINS, TUBES, and BOWLS, and reports the Chamfer Distance metric. It relies on FOUNDATIONPOSE for alignment of dagger-marked methods and includes V2I ATTENTION as a component. AMODAL3R is a dagger-marked baseline paired with FOUNDATIONPOSE. Procedural modeling code generates geometry using explicitly specified primitives, mesh operations, curves, modifiers, and procedural materials. Confidence-weighted physical ordering uses input object sets, ground root, and weighted edges.

## TETRIS3D is the central 3D scene generation method

TETRIS3D: 3D SCENE GENERATION WITH OBJECTS THAT FIT TOGETHER is a named method/framework introduced in a paper of the same title, designed to create scenes where objects are arranged to fit together cohesively [Data: Entities (102)]. It serves as the central entity connecting multiple technical components and external tools. The method uses Blender for constructing scenes through agent-authored procedural modeling code and executes modeling and rendering on the CPU [Data: Relationships (415, 416)]. It also reports the Chamfer Distance metric defined in equation (8) [Data: Relationships (356); Entities (283)]. This centrality suggests TETRIS3D integrates rendering, alignment, and geometric containment primitives into a unified pipeline.

## Blender and CPU provide the execution environment

BLENDER is procedural modeling and rendering software that provides an editable Blender scene and is used for creating and rendering 3D content [Data: Entities (268)]. TETRIS3D uses Blender to construct scenes through agent-authored procedural modeling code [Data: Relationships (415)]. CPU serves as execution hardware for modeling and rendering [Data: Entities (327)] and is used by TETRIS3D to execute modeling and rendering [Data: Relationships (416)]. Together, these entities form the computational backbone of the community's scene generation workflow.

## Containment object primitives are core components of TETRIS3D

TETRIS3D includes multiple containment object types and parametric primitive types as components: CUPS, OPEN BINS, POLYGONAL BINS, TUBES, and BOWLS [Data: Relationships (332, 333, 334, 335, 336); Entities (256, 257, 258, 254, 259)]. These primitives function both as practical containers for physical or digital items and as configurable geometric elements within a modeling or design system. Their inclusion indicates that the method emphasizes structured object arrangement and spatial cohesion in generated scenes.

## FOUNDATIONPOSE and V2I ATTENTION support alignment and amodal completion

FOUNDATIONPOSE is an alignment tool developed by Wen et al. in 2024, used to align generated objects to the scene, and is required specifically for dagger-marked methods [Data: Entities (107)]. TETRIS3D reports that FOUNDATIONPOSE is an alignment tool required only for dagger-marked methods [Data: Relationships (179)]. V2I ATTENTION is a named method component from section 3.3 and is part of the paper's method as a has_component relationship [Data: Entities (103); Relationships (98)]. These components enable precise object placement and visible-to-invisible attention for amodal completion within the generation pipeline.

## AMODAL3R is a dagger-marked baseline paired with FOUNDATIONPOSE

AMODAL3R is an amodal generation baseline method marked with a dagger, serving as a baseline for amodal generation and pose estimation as indicated in Table 4 [Data: Entities (125)]. It provides an occlusion-aware attention module referenced in ablation studies [Data: Entities (125)]. AMODAL3R generates objects aligned to a scene using FoundationPose and is paired with FoundationPose for placement in the scene [Data: Relationships (146)]. This relationship highlights FOUNDATIONPOSE's role as a shared alignment dependency across multiple methods in the community.

## Procedural modeling code constructs geometry through multiple operations

PROCEDURAL MODELING CODE is agent-authored code for constructing scenes [Data: Entities (328)]. It uses explicitly specified primitives, mesh operations, curves, modifiers, and procedural materials to create geometry [Data: Relationships (420, 421, 422, 423, 424); Entities (329, 330, 331, 332, 333)]. These relationships show that scene construction in Blender is driven by code that combines geometric primitives with material and mesh processing capabilities.

## Confidence-weighted physical ordering uses structured inputs

CONFIDENCE-WEIGHTED PHYSICAL ORDERING is Algorithm 1, a named method [Data: Entities (272)]. It uses OBJECTS V as an input object set, GROUND ROOT R as an input ground root, and ED={(VJ→VI,W)} as input edges with weights [Data: Relationships (346, 347, 348); Entities (273, 274, 275)]. These inputs suggest the algorithm orders objects based on confidence-weighted physical relationships within a scene graph structure.

The community centers on 3D scene generation methods and their evaluation metrics, with SAM-3D and Tetris3D configurations as key entities. SAM-3D serves as a central baseline method reporting numerous reconstruction, physical stability, and generation quality metrics across MessyKitchens and Picasso datasets. Tetris3D-derived configurations, including W/ AMODAL3R ATTN and W/O INTERACTION COND., are constructed from TETRIS3D and evaluated on Toys4K. The network connects methods to metrics through reporting relationships, while metrics like P-FID depend on components such as Point-E.

## SAM-3D as a central baseline method

SAM-3D is a scene generation baseline method evaluated in Table 2 and listed in the Method column of Table 1. It serves as a baseline method in Table 4 and is compared as a method in Tab. 4. Additionally, SAM-3D is identified as a scene generation baseline method [Data: Entities (106)]. SAM-3D reports a wide range of metrics including CD-S on MessyKitchens, CD-O on Picasso, F1-S on MessyKitchens and Picasso, F1-O on both datasets, IOU-B on both datasets, ICP-ROT on both datasets, PD on both datasets, DMEAN on both datasets, EPEAK on both datasets, MMD, COV, UNI3D, and ULIP [Data: Relationships (102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 113, 114, 115, 108, 109, 111, 112)]. This extensive reporting network positions SAM-3D as a central node connecting multiple evaluation dimensions.

## Tetris3D-derived configurations and attention mechanisms

W/ AMODAL3R ATTN is a configuration that replaces V2I attention with the Amodal3R attention module, specifically utilizing the Amodal3R occlusion-aware attention module to handle occluded objects more effectively [Data: Entities (162)]. This configuration is constructed from TETRIS3D [Data: Relationships (250)]. W/O INTERACTION COND. is an ablation configuration without interaction conditioning, also derived from TETRIS3D [Data: Entities (161); Relationships (249)]. W/ AMODAL3R ATTN uses the OCCLUSION-AWARE ATTENTION MODULE from Amodal3R [Data: Relationships (284); Entities (163)]. These configurations represent variations of the Tetris3D system with different attention and conditioning mechanisms.

## Reconstruction quality metrics network

The community includes multiple reconstruction quality metrics that evaluate surface and geometric fidelity. CD-S is a scene-level Chamfer Distance for surface reconstruction quality, measuring Chamfer distance at the scene level by concatenating point sets of all objects within a scene [Data: Entities (109)]. CD-O measures object-level Chamfer distance, evaluating geometric fidelity of individual object reconstructions [Data: Entities (110)]. F1-S is a scene-level F1 score combining precision and recall derived by thresholding nearest-neighbour distances at τ [Data: Entities (111)]. F1-O is an object-level F1 score for object reconstruction quality [Data: Entities (112)]. IOU-B evaluates bounding box reconstruction accuracy through Intersection over Union [Data: Entities (113)]. ICP-ROT measures rotation error in 3D reconstruction processes using the Iterative Closest Point algorithm [Data: Entities (114)]. These metrics are reported by SAM-3D across MessyKitchens and Picasso datasets [Data: Relationships (102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107)].

## Physical stability metrics

The community incorporates physical stability metrics that quantify penetration, overlap, and displacement in 3D reconstructions. PD, or Penetration Depth, quantifies the extent of penetration or overlap between entities using the formula PD = 1/N ∑ᵢ₌₁ᴺ ∑ⱼ max{0, -ϕⱼ(xᵢ)}, with lower values indicating better physical stability [Data: Entities (120)]. DMEAN, also known as Mean Distance metric, assesses physical stability with lower values indicating greater stability [Data: Entities (121)]. EPEAK, referred to as Peak Energy metric, follows a downward trend where lower values indicate better physical stability [Data: Entities (122)]. SAM-3D reports PD, DMEAN, and EPEAK metric values on both MessyKitchens and Picasso datasets [Data: Relationships (113, 114, 115)].

## Generation quality metrics and dependencies

Generation quality metrics evaluate generative models against ground-truth object distributions. MMD measures generative quality by comparing the distribution of generated data against ground-truth object distribution, reported in units of 10⁻³ [Data: Entities (115)]. COV measures coverage by calculating the fraction of ground-truth objects selected as the nearest neighbor of at least one generated object [Data: Entities (116)]. P-FID calculates the Fréchet distance between distributions of generated and ground-truth objects in the feature space of the point-cloud feature extractor released with Point-E [Data: Entities (117)]. P-FID uses the point-cloud feature extractor released with Point-E [Data: Relationships (358); Entities (291)]. UNI3D and ULIP evaluate semantic alignment between input images and generated point clouds [Data: Entities (118, 119)]. SAM-3D reports MMD, COV, UNI3D, and ULIP [Data: Relationships (108, 109, 111, 112)].

## Scene generation baseline methods and dataset evaluations

Multiple scene generation baseline methods are evaluated on specific datasets. WORLDSCULPT extends Pixal3D to a multi-view setting for scene-level generation and was evaluated on Toys4K [Data: Entities (124); Relationships (131)]. SHAPER is a baseline method included in Table 4 and compared in Table 1, evaluated on Toys4K [Data: Entities (123); Relationships (116)]. SCENEGEN is a scene generation baseline method listed in Table 2, reporting CD-S on both MessyKitchens and Picasso [Data: Entities (130); Relationships (192)]. SCENEMAKER is a scene generation baseline method evaluated on MessyKitchens [Data: Entities (131); Relationships (202)]. MIDI is a scene generation baseline method reporting CD-S on MessyKitchens [Data: Entities (129); Relationships (182)]. OURS (VLM), a configuration of Tetris3D using VLM-inferred relations, was evaluated on Toys4K [Data: Entities (295); Relationships (366)]. GENA3D is an amodal generation and pose estimation method requiring alignment using FoundationPose [Data: Entities (126); Relationships (148)].

## Comparative performance across methods

SAM-3D and UNI3D are evaluated using multiple 3D generation metrics, with SAM-3D reporting higher Uni3D and ULIP scores compared to UNI3D. However, UNI3D achieves the best performance in MMD, COV, and P-FID metrics [Data: Relationships (111)]. Similarly, SAM-3D achieves higher scores in both Uni3D and ULIP compared to another method, while that other method attains the best results in MMD, COV, and P-FID [Data: Relationships (112)]. This indicates that each model excels in different aspects of 3D generation quality, with no single method leading across all measured metrics.

# Optimal Topological Sort and Interaction-Specific Placement

The community centers on two primary computational methods: Optimal Topological Sort and Interaction-Specific Placement. Optimal Topological Sort serves as a central algorithm that uses a wide array of data structures and graph properties to compute generation order from physical dependency edges. Interaction-Specific Placement defines and utilizes predefined physical interaction types such as STACK, LEAN, CONTAIN, TOUCH, and PILE to generate scenes with predefined interactions. These entities are interconnected through usage relationships that define how the algorithms operate on scene data and physical relations.

## Optimal Topological Sort as central algorithm

Optimal Topological Sort is the central entity in this community, with a degree of 21, indicating it is highly connected to other entities. It is an algorithm for computing generation order from physical dependency edges. The algorithm uses Plane as a root node and operates on a physical dependency hierarchy composed of directed load-bearing edges and undirected contact edges among scene objects. [Data: Entities (309); Relationships (395, 403)]

## Input data structures for topological sort

Optimal Topological Sort relies on several input data structures to perform its computation. It uses the color instance-segmentation image, object inventory JSON, and original RGB scene image as inputs. These data sources provide the visual and descriptive information necessary for physical dependency reasoning. [Data: Relationships (400, 401, 402)]

## Graph properties and state management

The algorithm utilizes specific graph properties and state variables to manage the sorting process. It uses in-degree to identify the root node and maintains possiblePredecessors for each vertex. The process involves states such as startState containing only Plane and fullState containing all objects. Additionally, it records parent vertices and maintains cost for each state during processing. [Data: Relationships (405, 406, 407, 408, 411, 412)]

## Cost computation and edge deletion

Optimal Topological Sort computes deletionCost for directed edges during state processing, which is the sum of confidences of directed edges deleted. It uses confidence values associated with physical dependency edges to determine the cost of edge deletion. This mechanism allows the algorithm to optimize the topological order based on edge reliability. [Data: Relationships (404, 409); Entities (316, 321)]

## Color and format specifications

The community includes specifications for color formats and data serialization used in the pipeline. RGB is the color format used in instance segmentation and object inventory, while JSON is the format used for object inventory entries. Optimal Topological Sort uses both RGB color format and JSON format for object inventory. [Data: Entities (325, 326); Relationships (413, 414)]

## Interaction-Specific Placement and predefined interactions

Interaction-Specific Placement is a method for generating scenes with predefined interactions, with a degree of 6. It uses several predefined interaction types including STACK, LEAN, CONTAIN, TOUCH, and PILE. STACK is characterized by a directed physical relation where object A relies on object B for support. LEAN is a directed physical relation where object A relies on object B for support. CONTAIN establishes a dependency where one object is supported or held by another. TOUCH is an undirected physical contact relation that does not involve load-bearing support. PILE is also a predefined interaction type. [Data: Entities (261, 262, 263, 264, 266, 265); Relationships (338, 339, 340, 342, 341)]

## Physical dependency hierarchy components

The physical dependency hierarchy is a key structure in this community, representing a hierarchy of directed load-bearing edges and undirected contact edges among scene objects. The ground plane node serves as a foundational element in this hierarchy. The hierarchy is used by Optimal Topological Sort to determine the generation order of objects based on their physical dependencies. [Data: Entities (314, 310); Relationships (403, 395)]

# TRELLIS.2 and TETRIS3D 3D Generation Community

The community centers on TRELLIS.2, a 3D shape generation framework, and TETRIS3D, a geometrically and physically coherent 3D scene generation method. TRELLIS.2 uses DINOV3 for image features, flow-matching formulation, and diffusion transformer architecture, while generating sparse structure and structured latents. TETRIS3D incorporates pose-aligned object generation, which uses object grid G. Object grid G serves as a spatial framework for conditions cimg, cdepth, and cint, and is associated with invisible and visible token sets. V2I cross-attention and cross-attention layers update occluded regions using visible tokens.

## TRELLIS.2 as a central 3D shape generation framework

TRELLIS.2 is a 3D shape generation framework that utilizes a two-stage pipeline with a 30-block DiT backbone for each generation stage. It employs a voxel-based generative backbone also used by TETRIS3D. TRELLIS.2 uses DINOV3 as a frozen image encoder for patch features and input image features, and as a feature map tool to construct voxel-wise conditions. Each stage is modeled with flow-matching formulation and by a diffusion transformer architecture. TRELLIS.2 first generates the sparse structure, a binary occupancy grid outlining coarse geometry. [Data: Entities (16, 26, 27, 28, 29); Relationships (22, 17, 20, 21)]

## TETRIS3D and pose-aligned object generation

TETRIS3D is a method for 3D scene generation that ensures both geometric and physical coherence. A key subsection within this work focuses on pose-aligned object generation in the scene, which is integral to the overall method. Pose-aligned object generation uses object grid G, a schematic grid corresponding to voxels that serves as the spatial framework on which cimg, cdepth, and cint are defined, and is associated with pose-aligned generation. [Data: Entities (57, 58, 59); Relationships (42, 43)]

## Object grid G and condition definitions

Object grid G is a schematic grid described in Section 3.2.1, corresponding to voxels. It serves as the spatial framework on which cimg, cdepth, and cint are defined. Cimg is an image condition defined on object grid G, cdepth is a depth condition defined on object grid G, and cint is a condition defined on object grid G. These conditions are constructed from object grid G. [Data: Entities (59, 89, 90, 91); Relationships (81, 82, 83)]

## Invisible and visible token sets with occlusion handling

Object grid G tokens form the invisible token set, which consists of tokens whose voxels lie along camera rays through occlusion pixels. The visible token set includes all remaining tokens not in the invisible token set. An occlusion mask treats all pixels occupied by other objects as potential occlusions of the target and defines the invisible token set. V2I cross-attention is an explicit mechanism that updates occluded parts using information aggregated from visible tokens, guiding the completion of occluded regions. [Data: Entities (99, 100, 98, 38); Relationships (95, 97, 32)]

## Cross-attention layers and structured latents

A cross-attention layer uses invisible tokens as queries and visible tokens as keys and values, with additional cross-attention layers supporting this mechanism. VSLAT Θ is a DiT model component that functions as a DiT layer component for structured latent generation, operating as a second diffusion transformer to process only active voxels. It generates structured latents, which are latent encodings attached to active voxels encoding geometry and texture. SLAT is the latent encoding of the O-Voxel representation, a field-free sparse voxel structure encoding geometry and appearance jointly. [Data: Entities (101, 34, 30, 31); Relationships (93, 94, 24, 19)]

## Image condition masking and VSS Θ

Image condition masking is a technique blending DINOv3 patch features with a learnable null embedding based on occlusion ratio, and it uses DINOV3. VSS Θ is a DiT model component and DiT layer component designed for sparse structure generation, functioning as the first diffusion transformer to denoise a dense latent volume on a coarse grid. [Data: Entities (219, 26, 33); Relationships (307, 23)]}],

# VLM Relation Graphs, Simulation, and Physical Plausibility

The community consists of three entities: VLM Relation Graphs, Physical Plausibility, and Simulation. VLM Relation Graphs and Simulation are tools used to enforce Physical Plausibility, which is a property designed to avoid physically implausible artifacts such as penetration or floating. The relationships indicate that both tools are used to refine poses or run in the loop to maintain this property.

## VLM Relation Graphs as a tool for physical plausibility

VLM Relation Graphs is a tool used to refine poses at test time to enforce physical plausibility. It has a direct relationship with Physical Plausibility, indicating its role in avoiding physically implausible artifacts such as penetration or floating. [Data: Entities (176); Relationships (299)]

Simulation is a tool run in the loop to enforce physical plausibility. It shares the same target as VLM Relation Graphs, suggesting that both tools serve a similar purpose in maintaining physical plausibility within a system. [Data: Entities (177); Relationships (300)]

Physical Plausibility is a property enforced to avoid physically implausible artifacts such as penetration or floating. # Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection and Its Components

The community centers on Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection, a condition injection mechanism that serves as a parent entity with three direct components: Image-Conditioned Update, ΛDepth, and ΛInt. These relationships indicate a modular technical architecture where Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection aggregates specialized sub-components, including two learnable scalar gates initialized to zero.

## Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection as the central mechanism

Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection is the primary entity in this community, described as a condition injection mechanism with a degree of 4, indicating multiple connections within the network. It functions as the parent or container for the other three entities, serving as the central node around which this technical community is organized. [Data: Entities (92); Relationships (87, 88, 89)]

## Image-Conditioned Update as a direct component

Image-Conditioned Update is included as a component of Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection through a HAS_COMPONENT relationship. This entity is described as an image-conditioned update and has a degree of 1, suggesting it is a leaf node connected only to the parent mechanism. Its inclusion indicates that the condition injection mechanism processes or incorporates image-conditioned updates as part of its operation. [Data: Entities (95); Relationships (87)]

## ΛDepth as a learnable scalar gate component

ΛDepth is a learnable scalar gate initialized to zero and is included as a component of Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection. With a degree of 1, it represents a specialized parameter or gating mechanism within the broader condition injection framework. The zero initialization suggests it may serve as a trainable parameter that starts in a neutral or inactive state before learning. [Data: Entities (96); Relationships (88)]

## ΛInt as a learnable scalar gate component

ΛInt is also a learnable scalar gate initialized to zero and is included as a component of Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection. Like ΛDepth, it has a degree of 1 and represents another trainable scalar parameter within the mechanism. The presence of two distinct learnable scalar gates suggests the condition injection mechanism employs multiple gating strategies for controlling information flow or conditioning. [Data: Entities (97); Relationships (89)]

## Modular HAS_COMPONENT architecture

The community exhibits a clear hierarchical structure where Voxel-Aligned Condition Injection has three direct HAS_COMPONENT relationships to Image-Conditioned Update, ΛDepth, and ΛInt. All three relationships share a combined degree of 5, indicating strong connectivity between the parent and its components. This modular design suggests the condition injection mechanism is composed of interchangeable or specialized sub-units that work together to perform condition injection. [Data: Relationships (87, 88, 89)]
